features.name: Init Fwd Win Byts
features.description: Initial TCP window bytes in forward direction; typically -1 when unrecorded.
features.implication: Anomalous or absent forward window values can flag scanning or attack tools.

features.name: Tot Fwd Pkts
features.description: Total number of packets transmitted in the forward direction from source to destination.
features.implication: High forward packet counts with few backward packets are consistent with one-sided flooding.

features.name: Flow Pkts/s
features.description: Total packets transferred in both directions divided by flow duration in seconds.
features.implication: Very high rates are consistent with packet flooding; very low rates with slow or stalled flows.

features.name: Flow IAT Std
features.description: Standard deviation of inter-arrival times between consecutive packets in both directions.
features.implication: Low IAT variability can be consistent with machine-generated uniform flooding traffic.

features.name: Tot Bwd Pkts
features.description: Total number of packets transmitted in the backward direction from destination to source.
features.implication: Near-zero backward packet count is consistent with unanswered DoS flooding traffic.

Stateless protocols such as UDP or ICMP are commonly used but stateful protocols such as TCP can be used as well. Botnets are commonly used to conduct network flooding attacks against networks and services. Large botnets can generate a significant amount of traffic from systems spread across the global Internet.
